articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 security fixes including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. When even Patch Tuesday needs a forklift, you know we're living in interesting times.

articles.title: A “Scheme” Against Dobbs: SCOTUS Dissent Hints at Next Phase of Abortion Rights Fight
articles.summary: Another CVSS 10.0 Cisco SD-WAN bug gets exploited in the wild—second one this year. Cisco's network gear is becoming more reliable than a casino slot machine, except the house always loses.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas education platform gets pwned, disrupting schools nationwide with ransom demands on the login page. Nothing says 'back to school' like having your homework held hostage by cybercriminals.

articles.title: MPs want social media treated more like unsafe toys than harmless apps
articles.summary: OpenAI employees got malware from poisoned npm packages, leading to credential theft. Even the AI overlords can't resist clicking on suspicious links—there's hope for humanity yet.

articles.title: Canvas Hack Aftermath: Congress Wants Instructure to Answer Questions
articles.summary: TeamPCP hackers are auctioning off Mistral AI's source code like it's a vintage Pokemon card collection. The commoditization of AI breaches continues apace.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram kills its end-to-end encryption feature after years of promises, because apparently privacy is too hard for Meta. Another day, another betrayal from the Zuckerverse.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Apple finally enables end-to-end encryption for RCS messaging with Android. Only took them until 2026 to stop treating cross-platform privacy like a competitive disadvantage.

articles.title: The Boring Stuff is Dangerous Now
articles.summary: EFF launches campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid, imprisoned for the crime of believing information should be free. Twelve years old when he started editing Wikipedia—a digital freedom fighter from childhood.

articles.title: For ‘Survivor’ Legends Who Keep Coming Back, Outplaying and Outlasting Is a ‘Religious Experience’
articles.summary: Pwn2Own Berlin Day 2 nets researchers $385,750 for 15 zero-days, bringing the total to nearly $1M in bounties. The annual celebration of responsible disclosure and capitalism working in harmony.

articles.title: aegis-atv 0.5.1
articles.summary: AI-powered security research creates first Apple M5 memory exploit, bypassing Memory Integrity Enforcement for root access. When the machines start hacking themselves, we've truly entered the endgame.
